name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity / Random Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity
details: For finite concept classes and every fixed admissible counterexample distribution $\mu$.
proof: Fix $\mu$ as in the definition of random proper equivalence-query complexity. A proper equivalence-query strategy that identifies every target against every legal adversarial counterexample remains correct when each failed proposal receives a counterexample sampled from $\mu$ conditioned on its disagreement with the target. For each target, its expected query count under this law is at most its adversarial worst-case query count. Minimizing over strategies gives $\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{rpeq}}(\mathcal H;\mu)\le\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{peq}}(\mathcal H)$. This comparison concerns random counterexamples, not an enlargement of the learner by internal randomization.
